package_info.package_manager: kernel source (not a package manager, but distributed via Linux distributions)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected Linux kernel versions contain a vulnerability (Dirty Pipe, CVE-2022-0847) that allows unprivileged users to write arbitrary data to any file they can read, enabling privilege escalation and container escape. Exploitation code leverages this flaw to overwrite critical system files or binaries, resulting in full system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (local exploit execution by unprivileged user)
execution_context.file_location: user-supplied exploit code (typically a C program or PoC script run on the vulnerable system)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code is executed by an unprivileged user, uses the splice system call to manipulate the Linux kernel page cache, transfers data from a read-only file descriptor to a pipe, and then writes arbitrary data into the pipe to overwrite the contents of /etc/passwd, resulting in privilege escalation by enabling the attacker to add or modify root user entries.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unprivileged users should not be able to write to protected files like /etc/passwd. The exploit abuses the splice syscall and PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE to bypass normal write restrictions, which is highly abnormal and indicative of an exploit.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, only privileged users (root) can modify /etc/passwd or other protected files. This exploit allows unprivileged users to do so by exploiting a kernel vulnerability.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: The splice syscall is legitimately used for efficient data transfer between file descriptors, such as in high-performance servers, but never for modifying protected files like /etc/passwd by unprivileged users.
key_indicators: splice system call used on non-world-writable files such as /etc/passwd
PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE flag manipulation to enable unauthorized writes
write operations to /etc/passwd by non-root processes
creation and use of pipes in conjunction with splice and write to overwrite protected files

execution_context.trigger: runtime (local exploit execution from within a container)
execution_context.file_location: user-supplied exploit code (run inside a container)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code is executed from within a container, uses the splice system call to manipulate the kernel page cache, transfers data from the host's RunC binary to a pipe, and then writes a malicious payload into the pipe to overwrite /usr/bin/runc, resulting in the ability to execute arbitrary code on the host and escape the container.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Containerized processes should not be able to modify host binaries. Overwriting RunC from a container is a clear sign of a container escape attempt and indicates a severe breach of container isolation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Containers are expected to be isolated from the host and not able to alter host binaries. This exploit breaks that isolation by allowing modification of /usr/bin/runc from within a container.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate scenario where a container process overwrites the host's RunC binary. System updates to RunC are performed by privileged host processes, not by containerized code.
key_indicators: splice system call targeting executable files in /usr/bin or similar host paths from within a container
PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE flag manipulation to enable unauthorized writes
modification of container runtime binaries (e.g., /usr/bin/runc) by non-root or containerized processes
write operations to host binaries initiated from containerized environments

execution_context.file_location: user-supplied exploit code (targeting any critical system file)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code is executed by an unprivileged user, uses the splice system call to manipulate the kernel page cache, transfers data from a read-only system binary to a pipe, and then writes malicious code into the pipe to overwrite files in critical system paths (e.g., /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin), resulting in the replacement of system binaries with attacker-controlled payloads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Overwriting system binaries by unprivileged users is a clear privilege escalation and persistence technique, as it allows attackers to replace trusted executables with malicious code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Only privileged users should be able to modify system binaries. This exploit allows non-root users to overwrite executables in protected directories, violating core system security assumptions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System updates or package installations by root may legitimately overwrite these files, but unprivileged users should never be able to do so.
key_indicators: splice system call on files in /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /usr/local/bin, /usr/local/sbin, /boot
PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE flag manipulation to enable unauthorized writes
modification of executable files by non-root users
write operations to system binaries by processes without elevated privileges

attack_chain.action: Attacker runs exploit code as an unprivileged user or from within a container, targeting a protected file or binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary write access to files readable by the attacker (e.g., /etc/passwd, /usr/bin/runc, system binaries).

attack_chain.action: Exploit code uses the splice syscall with PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE to manipulate the kernel page cache and overwrite target file contents.
attack_chain.leads_to: Privilege escalation (e.g., new root user in /etc/passwd), container escape (overwriting RunC), or replacement of system binaries with malicious payloads.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains elevated privileges or escapes the container, achieving full system or host compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: root access, host takeover, or persistent compromise via modified system binaries.

behavioral_signatures: splice system call used by unprivileged users on files that are not world-writable
splice with PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE flag set to enable unauthorized writes
write operations to critical system files (e.g., /etc/passwd, /bin/*, /usr/bin/runc) by non-root users
modification of system binaries or container runtime binaries from containerized processes
file_indicators: executables in /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /usr/local/bin, /usr/local/sbin, /boot modified by non-root users
/usr/bin/runc or other container runtime binaries altered from within a container
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the splice system call being used by unprivileged users on files that are not world-writable, especially when the PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE flag is set. Use eBPF, auditd, or similar frameworks to track these syscall patterns in real time. Alert on any attempts to modify critical system files (e.g., /etc/passwd, system binaries, container runtime binaries) by non-root users or from within containers. Correlate write operations to protected files with the absence of root privileges to identify exploitation attempts.
